info.name: chatty
info.description:
All routes in chatty-core and chatty-chat.

1. Select the "Chatty local" environment (chatty-local.postman_environment.json).
2. Run Auth > register once, then login. Login saves access_token and refresh_token.
3. Internal uses service_token from the environment: the dev default change-me. If chatty-infra/.env sets another CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN, use that.

The WebSocket (GET {{chat_url}}/api/chat/v1/ws?token={{access_token}}) can't be stored in a collection file: open it in Postman with New > WebSocket.

exec: // swap so login keeps working and the next run changes it back

request.description: Step 1 of an upload: a 5-byte text attachment, which the next two requests upload and confirm. For an avatar, use purpose "avatar", team_id null, an image mime and the image's exact size in bytes, then send the image file as a binary body in the PUT (confirm checks that the bytes really are that image). Saves file_id and upload_url.
Step 2: straight to MinIO. Content-Type and the body's length (5 bytes) must match mime and size from POST /files, or MinIO answers 403. Postman sets Content-Length itself.
Step 3: chatty-core checks the upload and marks the file ready. Sending it again also gives 200. Before the PUT: upload_missing; after 10 minutes: upload_expired.

Download an avatar or a team icon: 302 with a presigned GET URL in Location, valid 5 minutes. Redirects are not followed here, so you can see the 302; the URL is saved as download_url for the next request. The text attachment from POST /files gives 400 use_chatty_chat (attachments go through chatty-chat): upload an avatar first. Not ready, deleted or unknown: 404 file_not_found; a team icon of another team: 403 not_a_team_member.
The image itself, straight from MinIO, with the file's Content-Type and Content-Disposition inline. No Authorization header: the signature is in the URL. After 5 minutes MinIO answers 403.

Delete my own file that is in no message: 204, no body. Works for pending and ready files; the file and its upload are removed from MinIO. My current avatar is also removed from my profile (GET /me shows avatar_file_id null). A team's current icon is also removed from the team (icon_file_id null), but only if I am an owner or admin there, else 403 forbidden. Sending it again: 404 file_not_found. Someone else's file: 403 forbidden; a file in a message: 409 file_attached.

exec: // a new message each run; send it twice without this to see the retry (200)
// a new message each run; send it twice without this to see the retry (200)

request.description: A message with a file (D-03). Before: in the Files folder, POST /files (a text attachment of {{team_id}}), the PUT and confirm; that sets file_id. body may be empty when file_ids isn't. 201 with file_ids and attachments (file_id, filename, mime, size). Sending the same file in a new message: 400 invalid_file, the message names the file. The same file twice in file_ids: 400 validation_error. chatty-core down: 503 core_unavailable. Deleting the message (DELETE /messages/:message_id) detaches its files: attaching the file again (Internal folder) then gives 404.

Download URLs for the files of a message (D-02): one presigned MinIO URL per file, in the order they were sent, valid 5 minutes (expires_at). Run POST /channels/:channel_id/messages (with a file) first; it sets message_id. Saves the first URL as attachment_url. A message without files: attachments []. A deleted or unknown message, or a channel you can't read: 404 message_not_found.

The file itself, straight from MinIO, with its Content-Type and Content-Disposition: attachment and its filename. No Authorization header: the signature is in the URL. After 5 minutes MinIO answers 403; call GET /messages/:message_id/attachments again.

query.description: older than this seq; for scrolling up
required: the last seq the web app has

request.description: A seq past the channel's last message is lowered to it, so this marks the whole channel read.
Sample keys of the right length (p256dh 65 bytes, auth 16), not a real browser: the push worker's sends to this endpoint fail, and it deletes the subscription.

What chatty-chat calls before saving a message with files (D-03): all the files are attached, or none. Before: run GET /me (sets me_id), POST /teams (sets team_id and channel_id, the general channel), and the Files folder up to confirm with the default text attachment (sets file_id). 200 with object_key, filename, mime, size and attached_at for each file. Sending it again: 409 file_already_attached. An avatar: 400 wrong_purpose. A file that fails names it in error.fields.file_id. Not reachable through Nginx: call chatty-core directly.

What chatty-chat calls after a message with files is deleted, or after its save failed (D-03): the attachments are deleted. Always 204, also when nothing changed, so it can be retried. Unknown ids, deleted files, avatars and team icons are skipped. Afterwards, attach with the same file gives 404 file_not_found.
